auth_domain.description: The domain to authenticate users with when using App Engine's User API.
auth_domain.rationale: Sets the domain used to authenticate users via App Engine's legacy User API. It selects an identity domain rather than enabling or disabling a security control, and a generic policy cannot pin a domain (team/org-specific), so it is not a policy target.

database_type.description: The type of the Cloud Firestore or Cloud Datastore database associated with this application. Can be `CLOUD_FIRESTORE` or `CLOUD_DATASTORE_COMPATIBILITY` for new instances.  To support old instances, the value `CLOUD_DATASTORE` is accepted by the provider, but will be rejected by the API. To create a Cloud Firestore database without creating an App Engine application, use the [`google_firestore_database`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/google/latest/docs/resources/firestore_database) resource instead.
database_type.rationale: Selects whether the app uses Cloud Firestore or Datastore-compatibility mode. This is a team data-architecture choice, not a security control, and mandating one mode does not harden the resource.

location_id.description: The location to serve the app from.
location_id.rationale: Sets the region the App Engine application is served from. Region/data-residency is a sanctioned policy target: a policy should constrain it to an approved location whitelist (the value is immutable once set, so enforcing it at create time matters).

project.description: The project ID to create the application under.
project.rationale: Identifier of the GCP project that owns the application. This is a project reference; we do not constrain which project a resource belongs to, and the ID-vs-number distinction is a deployment-correctness concern, not security.

serving_status.description: The serving status of the app.
serving_status.rationale: The operational serving state of the application. This is an availability/operational toggle, not a security control, and no generic secure value can be enforced.

ssl_policy.description: The SSL policy that will be applied to the application. If set to Modern it will restrict traffic with TLS \u003c 1.2 and allow only Modern Ciphers suite
ssl_policy.rationale: To enforce secure managed SSL certificates to ensure all data in transit is encrypted using modern protocols and to prevent service outages caused by manual certificate expiration.

feature_settings.description: A block of optional settings to configure specific App Engine features:

feature_settings.split_health_checks.description: Set to false to use the legacy health check instead of the readiness and liveness checks.
feature_settings.split_health_checks.rationale: Toggles between split readiness/liveness health checks and the legacy combined check. This is a deployment-reliability/availability choice, not a security control.

iap.description: Settings for enabling Cloud Identity Aware Proxy

iap.enabled.description: Adapted for use with the app

iap.oauth2_client_id.description: OAuth2 client ID to use for the authentication flow.
iap.oauth2_client_id.rationale: Mandates a valid OAuth2 Client ID to securely link the IAP to the organization's identity provider, ensuring only verified corporate credentials can grant access.

iap.oauth2_client_secret.description: OAuth2 client secret to use for the authentication flow. The SHA-256 hash of the value is returned in the oauth2ClientSecretSha256 field.
iap.oauth2_client_secret.rationale: Ensures the authenticity of the handshake between Google Cloud and the Identity Provider to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks/unauthorized identity spoofing.
